original_evidence.text:
Studypages - Evaluation of a combination of three drugs in dogs with hemangiosarcoma
Skip to main content

registry_protocol_details.potential_benefits: Potential benefits include stronger response to the treatment protocol, decreased risk of metastasis, and improved survival time.
registry_protocol_details.potential_risks:
Poor response to treatment

Higher than described adverse effects from combination treatment (nausea, diarrhea, weight loss, bone marrow suppression, illness requiring hospitalization and management)
registry_protocol_details.inclusion_criteria:
1. Biopsy confirmed hemangiosarcoma 
  2. Life expectancy greater than 2 weeks 
  3. No major organ failure
registry_protocol_details.exclusion_criteria:
1. Evidence of renal or liver failure that precludes use of doxorubicin or carboplatin 
  2. Patients taking antioxidant supplements (or these may be discontinued during the study)
  3. Patients who have previously received both doxorubicin and carboplatin as part of their treatment (if they have received only one of the two options, then they can be considered for the other arm)
registry_protocol_details.pri_outcome_measure: Imaging will be used to monitor disease status and owner questionnaires (along with labwork and physical examinations) will be used to monitor dogs. Modified RECIST criteria will be used to characterize tumor response.
registry_protocol_details.pri_outcome_endpoint: The study will be halted for patients that experience progressive disease. Median time to progression and median survival times will be described. Owners may also elect to remove their dog from the study at any point.
registry_protocol_details.sec_outcome1_measure: VCOG-CAE 2020 will be used to measure and describe adverse events. Bloodwork, imaging, patient monitoring/examinations, and owner questionnaires will all be utilized to determine adverse events.
registry_protocol_details.sec_outcome1_endpoint: Dogs that experience high grade (grade 3-4) adverse events will have interventions to try to eliminate those adverse events (fluid therapy, hospitalization, medical management). Reduction of chemotherapy doses will be considered as well in order to improve tolerance of treatments. Dogs that experience a decline in heart function during doxorubicin treatment will no longer receive doxorubicin treatment but may be considered for the carboplatin arm.

protocol_content.name: Evaluation of a combination of three drugs in dogs with hemangiosarcoma
protocol_content.tagline: Combination therapy for dogs with Hemangiosarcoma
protocol_content.description: The objective of this study is to investigate the effectiveness of combining doxorubicin or carboplatin and temozolomide with propranolol in dogs with hemangiosarcoma. The use of either doxorubicin or carboplatin alone as a treatment for hemangiosarcoma has been studied, and studies with propranolol (historically used to treat heart disease) have shown promise as an added treatment against hemangiosarcoma, however, survival times still remain quite low. We are hopeful that survival times can be further improved using a combination approach to treatment, with combination of both intravenous and oral treatments. Dogs with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, liver, heart or intramuscular region will be considered for inclusion in this study.
